Fala de salário, férias e despedimento — mas também do primeiro contrato, do primeiro recibo e da primeira vez que alguém tenta convencer-te de que «é assim em todo o lado». Dois andares: o essencial e o fundo. As regras do jogo. Nada a ganhar além de vocabulário. E uma ideia que vale mais que o resto: um contrato de trabalho não é um favor que te fazem — é uma relação com direitos dos dois lados, escrita na lei e não na simpatia do patrão. As outras partes. O Código Civil explica a vida em comum; o Código Penal explica o que acontece quando alguém passa a linha. Este é o código do dinheiro em troca de tempo. A quarta parte é a estrada : o movimento e quem tem prioridade. O que é o Código do Trabalho É a Lei n.º 7/2009, de 12 de fevereiro , e regula a relação entre quem trabalha e quem paga. Substituiu um código de 2003 que já tinha substituído outro de 1969 — três códigos em quarenta anos dizem muito sobre como esta matéria muda. O código não regula só o salário. Regula a idade com que se pode começar, o que tem de estar escrito no contrato, quantas horas se trabalha, quantos dias se descansa, o que acontece quando se adoece, o que acontece quando nasce um filho, e como se sai — por acordo, por decisão da entidade patronal, ou porque a empresa fechou. E tem uma característica que o torna diferente dos outros dois códigos desta série: aqui, a lei é um mínimo . Um contrato pode dar mais do que a lei; nunca menos. Perceber isto resolve metade das discussões sobre trabalho. A idade mínima A idade mínima para celebrar um contrato de trabalho em Portugal é 16 anos , e exige-se a escolaridade obrigatória concluída. Entre os 16 e os 18 há um regime próprio, com proteções que existem porque um jovem ainda está a crescer — física e mentalmente. Menores e trabalho Situação Regra Menos de 16 anos Não há contrato de trabalho 16 e 17 anos Contrato permitido, com autorização de quem representa o menor Trabalho noturno Proibido, em regra Trabalho perigoso ou insalubre Proibido Horas Limite mais baixo que o dos adultos Repara no que a lei faz: não proíbe trabalhar aos 16, proíbe explorar aos 16. A diferença entre as duas coisas está escrita em limites de horas, exames de saúde e tarefas interditas — não na boa vontade de ninguém. O contrato Um contrato de trabalho pode ser sem termo (o normal, sem data de fim) ou a termo (com data de fim, e só permitido quando existe um motivo previsto na lei, escrito no contrato). Há ainda o trabalho a tempo parcial, o estágio e o trabalho temporário, cada um com regras próprias. No início há o período experimental : um tempo em que qualquer das partes pode terminar sem justificação, precisamente porque ainda ninguém se conhece. Em regra são 90 dias no contrato sem termo; há prazos maiores em situações previstas (primeiro emprego, desemprego de longa duração) e mais curtos nos contratos muito curtos. O que deve estar escrito: identificação das partes, atividade, local, duração, retribuição, horário e data de início. O que não pode estar escrito: cláusulas que tirem direitos garantidos pela lei — mesmo que assines, não valem. Se te pedirem para assinar sem ler. Diz que lês em casa e que assinas amanhã. Um contrato que só se pode assinar «agora» é, quase sempre, um contrato que não sobrevive a uma leitura calma. O salário e o recibo Existe um salário mínimo nacional , fixado todos os anos pelo Governo. Nenhum contrato pode pagar abaixo disso — nem «à experiência», nem «à comissão» sem garantia, nem «em dinheiro e sem papéis». Do valor bruto ao que recebes há dois descontos obrigatórios: IRS (imposto sobre o rendimento, retido na fonte) e Segurança Social (11% a cargo de quem trabalha, 23,75% a cargo da entidade patronal, no regime geral). O recibo de vencimento tem de mostrar os dois, e mostrá-los é o que permite provar, anos depois, que trabalhaste. A isso juntam-se o subsídio de férias e o subsídio de Natal . E há regras para o trabalho suplementar (horas extra), para o trabalho noturno e para o descanso semanal — pagos ou compensados, não oferecidos como gentileza. O tempo O limite normal é de 40 horas por semana . Pode ser menor por contrato coletivo ou por acordo, nunca maior sem as regras do trabalho suplementar. As férias são de 22 dias úteis por ano, e os feriados não se descontam nelas. O descanso semanal é obrigatório; e existe um intervalo entre jornadas que serve para dormir, não para «ficar disponível». O teletrabalho trouxe uma figura que vale a pena conhecer: o direito à desconexão . Fora do horário, não tens de responder — e a entidade patronal não te pode penalizar por isso. Estar contactável 24 horas não é dedicação: é uma violação com nome. Adoecer Adoecer não é faltar. A baixa por doença é um direito, com atestado e comunicação à Segurança Social, e a lei protege o posto de trabalho durante esse período. Há também faltas justificadas por assistência à família, por luto, por casamento, por deveres cívicos e por exames. A regra prática: avisa, documenta, guarda o comprovativo . Um direito que não se prova é um direito que se discute. Ser pai ou mãe A lei dá licenças por parentalidade — 120, 150 ou 180 dias, conforme a escolha e a partilha entre os progenitores — e uma licença de paternidade com dias obrigatórios. Há ainda faltas para assistência a filhos, aleitação e consultas. Estas licenças não são «benefícios»: são a forma que a lei encontrou de impedir que ter filhos custe o emprego a uma pessoa e não custe nada à outra. Quem já viu uma mãe ser preterida por «ter filhos» sabe porque é que esta parte do código existe. Quando termina Por acordo: os dois lados concordam, e o acordo deve ser escrito. Por iniciativa do trabalhador: com aviso prévio, cujo prazo depende da antiguidade. Por facto imputável ao trabalhador: exige motivo grave, processo disciplinar e direito de resposta. Não é «hoje não gostei do teu tom». Por extinção do posto de trabalho ou despedimento coletivo: exige critérios objetivos, ordem e compensação. No período experimental: sem justificação, mas dentro dos prazos legais. Fora dessas portas, o despedimento é ilícito , e o trabalhador pode escolher entre a reintegração e uma indemnização. E há um prazo que se esquece com frequência: os créditos laborais prescrevem, em regra, num ano. Direitos que não se negoceiam Há matérias em que nem o acordo das duas partes serve para renunciar: Assédio (artigo 29.º): comportamento indesejado que humilha, constrange ou cria um ambiente hostil. É proibido, e é contraordenação muito grave. Discriminação por sexo, idade, origem, religião, deficiência, orientação sexual ou situação familiar. Segurança e saúde no trabalho: formação, equipamento, avaliação de riscos. Liberdade sindical e direito à greve , garantidos na Constituição. Retaliação por denunciar: quem reclama não pode ser tratado pior por isso. Se algo correr mal Primeiro, prova: recibos, horários, mensagens, contratos, testemunhas. Depois, a ordem que funciona: falar por escrito com a entidade patronal; reclamar no livro de reclamações (sim, também serve para isto); e, se continuar, a ACT — Autoridade para as Condições do Trabalho , que fiscaliza, e o tribunal do trabalho , que decide. Existe apoio judiciário para quem não pode pagar advogado, e os sindicatos prestam apoio jurídico a quem é filiado. Nada disto é gratuito em tempo: é gratuito em mito. Isto não é aconselhamento jurídico. É um resumo para leitores dos 12 aos 99 anos. Em qualquer caso concreto vale o texto oficial do Código do Trabalho, o contrato coletivo aplicável e, quase sempre, o conselho de quem sabe. Para ir mais fundo O essencial acima chega para não ser enganado. O que vem a seguir é o que os manuais tratam em capítulos: as fontes do direito do trabalho, os contratos coletivos, a caducidade, a mobilidade e o cálculo das compensações. As fontes, e a estranha hierarquia do trabalho No direito do trabalho, a lei é o mínimo , não o máximo. A ordem é: Constituição, Código do Trabalho, contratação coletiva (contratos e acordos coletivos negociados entre sindicatos e associações patronais), regulamento interno da empresa, e contrato individual. Cada nível pode melhorar o de cima; nenhum pode piorar. É o contrário da lógica das normas: aqui o mais pequeno é que protege. Dá-se o nome de IRCT (instrumento de regulamentação coletiva de trabalho) ao texto assinado entre as partes sociais. É por isso que duas pessoas com o mesmo cargo podem ganhar diferente: podem estar abrangidas por IRCT distintos. Caducidade, cessação e o que fica Caducidade é o fim automático (contrato a termo que chega ao fim, reforma, morte); cessação é o fim por ato. A distinção importa porque muda o que é devido: compensações, aviso prévio, férias não gozadas e proporcionais dos subsídios. Nas compensações, a conta parte da retribuição base e diuturnidades , multiplicada pelo número de anos — e não do valor que «dá jeito» incluir ou excluir. É aí que aparecem as diferenças de milhares de euros que ninguém reclama porque não sabe fazer a conta. Mobilidade, horários e o poder de direção A entidade patronal tem poder de direção : pode definir tarefas, horários e local. Mas esse poder tem limites escritos — mudar de local de trabalho a centenas de quilómetros, alterar horários de forma substancial ou mudar funções sem acordo não é «gestão», é alteração ilícita do contrato. E há figuras intermédias que é preciso saber nomear: jus variandi (pequenas alterações), teletrabalho , banco de horas , horário concentrado . Cada uma tem de estar prevista e tem limites. O que o recibo esconde Três linhas que raramente se leem: a categoria (que define o trabalho que efetivamente fazes), a antiguidade (que conta para compensações e promoções) e o horário contratual . Um recibo com categoria errada pode valer anos de diferenças salariais e, no fim, uma compensação calculada sobre o valor errado. Alíneas e remissões: a morada da lei Aqui, mais do que nos outros códigos, o endereço decide. «Artigo 112.º» não chega: o período experimental muda com o número, com o tipo de contrato e com a situação de quem assina. Uma alínea lida fora do número que a contém transforma uma exceção numa regra, e é assim que circulam as frases «a lei permite» quando a lei apenas permite num caso . Caso 1 — o período experimental que ninguém calculou Assinas um contrato sem termo. O artigo 112.º fixa o período experimental em 90 dias — mas o mesmo artigo tem números e alíneas que alargam esse prazo em situações específicas (primeiro emprego, desemprego de longa duração) e que o encurtam nos contratos de muito curta duração. Duas pessoas, o mesmo artigo, prazos diferentes: a diferença está no número e na alínea, não no artigo. Caso 2 — a remissão que manda no teu salário O contrato diz «a retribuição é a prevista no IRCT aplicável». Isto é uma remissão : o contrato não fixa o valor, manda ler outro texto. Quem só lê o contrato fica sem saber quanto ganha — e quem só lê o IRCT pode perder a cláusula mais favorável do contrato. A resposta exige os dois, e a regra é sempre: aplica-se o que for mais favorável a quem trabalha. Como uma lei cobre outras leis Constituição — direito ao trabalho, à retribuição, à segurança, à greve e à liberdade sindical. Código do Trabalho — o mínimo aplicável a todos. IRCT — o que os sindicatos e as patronais negociaram; pode ser melhor que o código. Contrato individual — pode ser melhor que o IRCT; nunca pior. Regulamento interno e prática da empresa — valem naquilo que não contrariem os níveis acima. Como não te perderes. Lê o artigo completo, não a frase que te mostraram. Verifica a data da última alteração do Código do Trabalho (muda todos os anos). Procura o IRCT da tua atividade antes de concluir que «a lei não obriga». It speaks of wages, holidays and dismissal — and of the first contract, the first payslip and the first time someone tries to convince you that «it is like that everywhere». Two floors: the essentials and the depths. The rules of the game. Nothing to win beyond vocabulary. And one idea worth more than the rest: a contract of employment is not a favour done to you — it is a relationship with rights on both sides, written in law and not in the boss's goodwill. The other parts. The Civil Code explains life in common; the Penal Code explains what happens when someone crosses the line. This is the code of money in exchange for time. Part four is the road : movement and who goes first. What the Labour Code is It is Law no. 7/2009 of 12 February , and it governs the relationship between those who work and those who pay. It replaced a 2003 code which had already replaced a 1969 one — three codes in forty years says a great deal about how fast this subject moves. The code regulates more than wages. It regulates the age at which you may start, what must be written in the contract, how many hours you work, how many days you rest, what happens when you fall ill, what happens when a child is born, and how you leave — by agreement, by the employer's decision, or because the company closed. And it has a feature that separates it from the other two codes in this series: here, the law is a floor . A contract may give more than the law; never less. Understanding that settles half of all arguments about work. The minimum age The minimum age to sign a contract of employment in Portugal is 16 , and compulsory schooling must be completed. Between 16 and 18 a special regime applies, with protections that exist because a young person is still growing — physically and mentally. Minors and work Situation Rule Under 16 No contract of employment 16 and 17 Contract allowed, with authorisation from the minor's representatives Night work Prohibited, as a rule Dangerous or unhealthy work Prohibited Hours A lower ceiling than for adults Notice what the law does: it does not forbid working at 16, it forbids exploiting at 16. The difference between the two is written in hour limits, health examinations and forbidden tasks — not in anyone's goodwill. The contract A contract may be open-ended (the norm, with no end date) or fixed-term (with an end date, allowed only where a ground set by law exists and is written into the contract). There is also part-time work, internship and temporary work, each with its own rules. At the start there is the probation period : a time when either side may end without justification, precisely because neither knows the other yet. As a rule 90 days for an open-ended contract; longer in stated situations (first job, long-term unemployment) and shorter for very short contracts. What must be written: the parties, the activity, the place, the duration, the pay, the schedule and the start date. What may not be written: clauses removing rights guaranteed by law — even if you sign, they do not stand. If you are asked to sign without reading. Say you will read it at home and sign tomorrow. A contract that can only be signed «now» is almost always a contract that does not survive a calm reading. Pay and the payslip There is a national minimum wage , set every year by the Government. No contract may pay below it — not «on trial», not «on commission» without a guarantee, not «in cash and without papers». From gross to net there are two mandatory deductions: income tax (withheld at source) and Social Security (11% for the worker, 23.75% for the employer, in the general regime). The payslip must show both, and showing them is what lets you prove, years later, that you worked. Add the holiday allowance and the Christmas allowance . And there are rules for overtime, night work and weekly rest — paid or compensated, not offered as a kindness. Time The normal limit is 40 hours per week . It may be lower by collective agreement or by agreement, never higher without the rules on overtime. Holidays are 22 working days a year, and public holidays do not count against them. Weekly rest is mandatory; and there is a minimum interval between working days that exists so you can sleep, not so you can stay «available». Telework brought a figure worth knowing: the right to disconnect . Outside your hours you do not have to answer — and the employer may not penalise you for it. Being reachable 24 hours a day is not dedication: it is a violation with a name. Getting ill Being ill is not being absent. Sick leave is a right, with a medical certificate and notification to Social Security, and the law protects your job during that period. There are also justified absences for family assistance, bereavement, marriage, civic duties and examinations. The practical rule: warn, document, keep the proof . A right you cannot prove is a right you will have to argue about. Being a parent The law provides parental leave — 120, 150 or 180 days, depending on the choice and on how it is shared between parents — and paternity leave with mandatory days. There are also absences for assisting children, breastfeeding and appointments. These leaves are not «benefits»: they are the way the law found to stop having children costing one person their job and costing the other nothing. Anyone who has seen a mother passed over for «having children» knows why this part of the code exists. When it ends By agreement: both sides agree, and the agreement should be in writing. On the worker's initiative: with notice, whose length depends on seniority. For a reason attributable to the worker: requires a grave ground, a disciplinary process and the right of reply. It is not «I did not like your tone today». By extinction of the post or collective dismissal: requires objective criteria, order and compensation. During probation: without justification, but within the legal periods. Outside those doors, the dismissal is unlawful , and the worker may choose between reinstatement and compensation. And there is a deadline people forget: labour claims lapse, as a rule, within a year. Rights you cannot waive Some matters cannot be renounced even by agreement between the two sides: Harassmen

obsdLearning: Monkey Blog PT EN Índice Descobri que o OpenBSD pode ser o meu sistema operativo principal Caso queira usar este sistema como Firewall, devia tentar usá-lo sem instalar software extra, para ter a certeza de que o meu «Router» está seguro. Mas, ao ler a documentação do OpenBSD, vejo que é possível usar este sistema como Desktop com Firefox e muito outro software que uso normalmente em Linux. De facto, posso até emular uma máquina Linux dentro do OBSD e correr as aplicações de que gosto que não estão no OBSD, para lhes aceder com facilidade. A popularidade deste sistema não é grande, e eu não procuro popularidade, mas estabilidade. Por omissão, se tentares usar o Firefox o sistema fica lento que dói e podes perguntar: «Mas porquê?». A resposta está nas configurações predefinidas com que o OBSD corre. Se as mudares, terás um «sistema rápido», sem ser lento que dói. Fica menos seguro? (provavelmente fica, mas se não estiveres a servir nenhum serviço público, não é grande problema mudar essas configurações.) Então comecei a tentar usar o 'vi' sem instalar o 'vim'. É um pouco estranho, já que há algumas diferenças, mas se souberes jogar com o Vim, o 'vi' será um pouco diferente, mas não muito. Não há navegador por omissão, por isso preciso de instalar um pacote mínimo, como o 'w3m' ou o 'elinks', que são os meus navegadores favoritos para o terminal. Com isto em mente, consigo configurar uma máquina para ser uma firewall dedicada, tendo outras que não são, mas Desktops. Infelizmente, pelo menos para mim, preciso de ter uma máquina dedicada a usar Linux, já que a aplicação Cloudflared para criar um túnel entre o meu servidor pessoal e os servidores da Cloudflare não corre em OBSD nem em FBSD. Nesse ponto, mantenho o sistema Linux mais acessível do mundo, que é (na minha opinião, o Debian). Posso corrê-lo numa VM ou numa Máquina dedicada. Para isto, prefiro mesmo dedicar uma Máquina, já que consigo correr todo o software necessário sem «hackear» o sistema para o fazer funcionar. Ao usar um Túnel, todo o tráfego é gerido pelo serviço que estamos a usar, não pelo OBSD. O facto fascinante é que não precisamos de abrir portas Extra para aceitar ligações do mundo exterior, e podemos validar todos os pedidos http usando a API da Cloudflare, para ter a certeza de que todas as ligações que aceitamos vêm de uma fonte de confiança. Os programadores estão integrados em projectos fantásticos, independentes do sistema principal do OBSD. Estas pessoas preocupam-se em criar um sistema estável e seguro e, com isso em mente, sinto-me seguro . Comecei a ler sobre a shell predefinida que usam, que é a Korn Shell , cuja documentação qualquer um encontra no site da IBM , e há outra comunidade chamada SpaceWorks que é uma fonte Fantástica de Informação e uma plataforma muito boa para esclarecer dúvidas. Nesta pesquisa sobre «como usar o OBSD» sem instalar (demasiado software extra), estou a aprender um pouco mais sobre o fluxo do OBSD. Por exemplo, gosto mesmo de saber a diferença entre pastas e ficheiros; como não descobri como configurar as cores dos ficheiros listados, posso usar (alias ls='ls -F') no .profile e, com isso, vejo se os ficheiros listados são ficheiros ou pastas. Seria o mesmo usando 'ls -p'. Enfim, gosto sempre de ter esta sensação de que estou a melhorar tudo o que sei, com algo que me dá uma nova sensação de estabilidade e segurança. Nada é indestrutível e nada é eterno, mas este projecto é feito por muitos utilizadores com muita experiência em C, C++, Rust, Go, Python, Perl e muitas outras linguagens que podem ser úteis em qualquer sistema. Continuo em dúvida sobre o que é melhor (entre VMMs puros ou Qemu). onovodespertar: Uma Crítica ao novo número da revista "O Novo Despertar" Esta revista tem alguns artigos, artigos esses que não vou mencionar, mas sim o artigo com o nome: "Quanto à Unidade Visível da Igreja, Em que Situação estamos?". Duas páginas que poderia escrevê-las aqui para melhor entendimento dos meus comentários. O que está em causa A pergunta do artigo é simples e antiga: se existe uma só Igreja, porque é que os crentes aparecem divididos em tantas comunidades que não se reconhecem entre si? A revista responde com a doutrina da unidade visível, ou seja, a ideia de que a unidade não é apenas espiritual, mas deve ser observável por quem olha de fora. É uma boa pergunta, e é por isso que merece uma resposta melhor do que a que costuma ser dada. Unidade não é uniformidade Quando se fala de unidade visível, o que se descreve quase sempre é uniformidade: a mesma liturgia, a mesma estrutura, a mesma autoridade. Mas duas pessoas que rezam com palavras diferentes podem estar a dizer a mesma coisa, e duas pessoas que rezam com as mesmas palavras podem estar a pensar em coisas opostas. openbsdCompilation: ↶ Home Field Manual OBC-5 · compilation from source OpenBSD Compilation for Developers Everything in one page: a tree, an obj directory, a kernel, the whole userland, one X, and all the traps that bite between two good builds. Written for people who read source code on purpose. kernel · userland · xenocara · ports · release vanilla JS · CSS3 · no dependencies progress lives in this browser 01 Why compile at all OpenBSD ships binaries and releases every six months, and for most machines sysupgrade is the correct answer. Compiling is the correct answer for other roles: Tracking fixes between releases: -stable exists precisely so you can build today's stability fixes on top of a released base, without moving to -current. -current developers and testers: the snapshot base plus a compiled tree is how the project eats its own food every day. If you compile -current you are implicitly volunteering as the tester. Custom-kernel work: drivers, kernel experiments or a smaller GENERIC for an odd machine. Ports work: the ports(7) system is designed to be driven from source on your own machine, and the maintainers' workflow (patches, make update-patches , bulk builders) assumes it. Building releases: make release produces the install media and the sets you supply to your own machines, the same way the project produces theirs. Note: compiling is not a security upgrade by itself. A random local build of -current is less trustworthy than a signed release. The difference is that you can read every line you run — which is the point. 02 The machine The complete build (kernel + userland + X + ports infrastructure) is not large by modern standards, but it is the sum of many small machines. Plan like this: Resource Minimum Comfortable Notes RAM 2–4 GB 8 GB+ Kernel link time is the memory peak; big ports can spike hard. Disk — source trees ~3 GB 4–5 GB src , xenocara , ports checkouts. Disk — build + product ~15 GB 25–40 GB /usr/obj , /usr/xobj , /usr/lobj , DESTDIR, RELEASEDIR, distfiles, packages. CPU anything “more cores” Base builds are largely serial by design; ports bulk builds parallelise much better. Two filesystem decisions pay for themselves immediately: Give /usr or, better, a dedicated /usr/obj partition room to breathe. Running out of space during make build is the beginner classic. Put the build output on your fastest disposable storage. obj directories exist to be deleted. doas and the shell you will live in Root does the installing; work can stay interactive. Check your privilege tool: $ grep root /etc/doas.conf permit persist :wheel Note: make build shells out and expects sudo -style elevation to work non-interactively. With doas, permit persist for your group is the smooth path; otherwise prefix with SUDO=doas . 03 Get a tree Everything starts from CVS. Pick an anoncvs server near you from the list on the project website, then check out the trees you need: # base source, the one everything else depends on $ cd /usr $ cvs -qd anoncvs@server/pub/OpenBSD-src checkout -P src # X11 sources (Xenocara) $ cvs -qd anoncvs@server/pub/OpenBSD-xenocara checkout -P xenocara # ports for third-party software $ cvs -qd anoncvs@server/pub/OpenBSD-ports checkout -P ports To update a tree later, move it forward instead of checking out over it: $ cd /usr/src $ cvs -q up -Pd Three ways to be slightly wrong Rule one: install the matching snapshot or release first . A -current tree compiled against an old base mixes header generations and behaves in ways that waste your weekend. sysupgrade to the matching snapshot before touching cvs. Note: on -stable, install each <nn>.patch file for your release before building; the patches are the errata with build instructions attached. Note: keep trees for different flavours separate. A -current workstation and a -stable server can live on one disk if their trees are separate, but they must not share obj output. 04 Branches of the same rock One CVS tree, three flavours, and the build steps differ mostly in what you expect from them: Flavour Tag / have Wait for it to be Get updates by -release the install media frozen syspatch only -stable -rstab from the release tag conservative cvs pull + recompile -current unstable HEAD fast-moving cvs pull + recompile + read current.html -stable: born from the release tag with bug fixes back-ported. API-stable enough that a running host keeps its promises across a rebuild. -current: where development happens. Between major ABI changes it will require bootstrapping steps; current.html on the website is the contract, read it before you pull, not after you break. Never mix a -current kernel with a -stable userland, or the other way. The libc/kernel ABI pair moves together. 05 Order of operations Source build is a dance with a fixed order. Skipping a step produces the famous “file not found but everything looks fine” classes of failure: 1 Snapshot or release base in place sysupgrade / syspatch first. The tree must match the day's base. 2 make obj Symlink mirrors for every object directory into /usr/obj , so binaries never pollute the source tree itself. 3 Kernel Either the whole make kernel or a configured variant. A KARL-linked kernel comes from the release machinery; a hand-built one gets you to work. 4 Includes and userland make includes (or a straight make build , which does it in order) puts fresh headers into /usr/include before anything else is compiled against them. 5 Xenocara Same idea, /usr/lobj + /usr/xobj , installed over the old X. 6 Ports / release Your target ports, or a whole make release run if you are producing install sets. Note: make obj is re-runnable and idempotent. When in doubt, rm -rf /usr/obj/* and run it again. It takes seconds; debugging a mixed build takes evenings. 06 Build the kernel The plain path that follows the source tree as written: # from a clean tree with objects made $ cd /usr/src $ make obj $ make kernel # builds every kernel flavor for your arch from the shared obj area Installing it by hand make kernel puts the result under /usr/obj/... . Move it into place and keep the old one bootable — the boot loader understands > -prefixed names like boot> boot #bsd.prev : $ doas cp /usr/obj/sys/arch/$(machine -i)/compile/GENERIC/bsd /bsd $ doas rm -f /obsd && doas ln /bsd /obsd $ doas reboot A custom kernel Copy the stock config out of the way, edit it, and build the same way the tree does: $ cd /usr/src/sys/arch/$(machine -i)/conf $ cp GENERIC.MP KLUDGE $ vi KLUDGE # keep the diff small and boring $ config KLUDGE $ cd ../compile/KLUDGE $ make clean && make Warn: do not blind-delete devices you actually use, and do not remove wd0* / sd0* -style disk nodes or things your filesystem depends on. A “lean” kernel that cannot read its own disk is a form of modern haiku. Why is my kernel bigger / smaller than the stock one? Options and drivers differ, and KARL (Kernel Address Randomization Link) pads the stock one deliberately. Functionally, a hand-built kernel is fine; release builds do the KARL pass (two links so symbol placement differs between snapshot kernels). If you care about matching the project's randomisation behaviour, build via make release hooks. 07 Build userland This is the long loop: libc , /bin , /usr/bin , daemons, the compiler toolchain. Give it hours, not minutes. $ cd /usr/src $ make obj # idempotent; re-run freely $ make includes # headers before things compiled against them $ doas make build # or: $ SUDO=doas make build What make build will do to your machine, roughly in order: make cleandir -adjacent cleanup of built objects, make includes into /usr/include , the compiler bootstrap dance, every library, binary and manual page for your host, system configuration updates where needed (run sysmerge if told). After it finishes with no errors, reboot into the new world and run sysmerge if prompted — config file differences land outside make's jurisdiction. Warn: interrupting make build is legal ( Ctrl+C ) but restarting requires a clean /usr/obj and a fresh make obj at minimum. The tree does not reliably resume mid-flight, and half-installed binaries hide trickier bugs than missing ones. 08 Build Xenocara X sources follow the same choreography with different directories. The bootstrap target makes the meta-tooling, then the build proceeds: $ cd /usr/xenocara $ make bootstrap $ make obj $ doas make build Object output lands in /usr/xobj , intermediate tools in /usr/lobj . Like the base tree, both are disposable. Note: build userland before X. Xenocara links against freshly built libraries; doing it backwards is one of the rare genuine ordering traps left in the flow. 09 Ports: the source of everything else ports(7) is the third-party build system. Unlike base, it is designed to be driven on your machine, and it has opinions about tarballs, checksums and privilege separation. One port, properly # find it $ cd /usr/ports $ make search key= example # download + checksum (this is what verifies against a known digest) $ cd editors/example $ doas make fetch # build and install; config files ask politely via sysmerge-style dialogs $ doas make install Everyday knobs that keep your tree clean: Knob Does WRKOBJDIR Where work directories are created (keep them off the tree disk). DISTDIR Where source tarballs accumulate (share it across machines). PKG_PATH For prebuilt packages, the counterpoint to ports: pkg_add is what make install compares itself against. FLAVOR Build variants declared by the port ( make show=FLAVORS lists them). Maintainer tooling make update-patches regenerates patches/ from your work/ volunteer edits — the polite way to feed fixes upstream. portcheck / port-lib-depends / make wantlib-args keep the metadata honest. dpb (from ports infrastructure) drives parallel dependency-aware builds — the same engine the bulk builders use. One machine, many cores, correct dependency order for free. Warn: never make install untrusted ports as root on your only machine. Port build code is software you have not read yet, running before you install it. Separate VM or builder account is the security advice both from the project and from this page. 10 Release engineering make release walks the whole tree and produces the install sets your install media consumes: base , comp , xbase , man , and the bsd -family kernels. This is where KARL happens too: the kernel is linked twice so each snapshot gets a different memory layout. $ cd /usr/src $ doas env DESTDIR=/dest RELEASEDIR=/rel make release # then the two extra passes that verify it $ doas env DESTDIR=/dest2 make release 'UPDATE= no' # see FAQ for exact knobs Honest advice: read release(8) before your first run and do the first release in a VM. The knobs (DESTDIR, RELEASEDIR, the check-passes) have changed shape between versions, and your reading of the manual is the only thing guaranteed to match the tree you checked out. Note: ports and xenocara have their own release flows ( dpb for ports packages, make release in xenocara). They compose with the base release but are their own documents. 11 Traps and their traps The failure modes are boringly repetitive. Recognising them by symptom saves an afternoon each: Symptom Usually Fixed by Compiler killed, cc1 OOM Not enough RAM for link time More RAM, or build on a machine with swap. /usr/obj: No space left mid-build Disk arithmetic was optimistic Move obj to a bigger fs; clean other obj dirs. make build fails in weird template files after a partial edit Mixed tree state, stale objects rm -rf /usr/obj/* , make obj , restart clean. Kernel boots, userland refuses to run Kernel/userland age mismatch Match with the same tree and the same base. make -j N breaks the base build Base Makefiles are not parallel Run them serially (ports and dpb parallelise instead). Timestamps confused, make loops forever Clock skew, NFS with bad timesource NTP the build host; local disks built better. The big one: a tree that is halfway between two CVS states is the single most common self-inflicted wound. If you pulled new source, start the build from the top of the ladder (obj → kernel → build), not from wherever the last failure stopped. 12 Cheat sheet # update a tree (-current) $ cd /usr/src && cvs -q up -Pd # the daily ladder $ make obj $ make kernel $ [install bsd] $ doas make build # X $ make bootstrap && make obj $ doas make build # one port $ cd /usr/ports/section/name $ doas make fetch install # maintainer round trip $ make extract $ make patch $ [edit work/] $ make update-patches # release $ doas env DESTDIR=... RELEASEDIR=... \ make release The three man pages worth keeping close: release(8) , ports(7) , afterboot(8) . And, of course, FAQ 5 (building) of the official documentation is the ground truth, written by the people running the builders. 13 Your build, day by day Progress below is stored in this browser ( localStorage ) only. Uncheck, re-check, close the page; it reopens where you left it. 0 / 12 RESET Matching snapshot/release installed ( sysupgrade / syspatch ) src , xenocara , ports checked out from a mirror that answers doas configured and tested for the group that builds Disk sized: /usr/obj , /usr/xobj , distfiles headroom checked make obj from a clean /usr/obj make includes (or knowledge that make build covers it) Kernel built and moved into /bsd with the old one kept Rebooted; boot> boot #bsd.prev escape hatch known make build completed with zero errors sysmerge run (or confirmed clean) Xenocara: bootstrap → obj → build in that order First port built on a disposable account or VM
openbsdDesktop: ↶ Home Field Manual OBS-7 · desktop values that survive OpenBSD for Desktops The default install guards the machine like a server. A desktop needs the same discipline with roomier ceilings — enough that Firefox plays a video while the system keeps answering, without a single change that cannot be undone by deleting one line. sysctl · sndiod · firefox · wsconsctl · apm vanilla JS · CSS3 · no dependencies every knob is reversible 01 The deal The stock values of a fresh install are chosen to protect machines you never look at. That is why a browser can open too many files and fail, or a media pipeline can exhaust the process ceiling while the desktop crawls. The project itself documents this: the values exist so a runaway service eats the “small” quota first. The deal you are signing when you keep reading: Reversibility first. Most of this page is sysctl at runtime. Reboot clears it if you regret it. Persistence is a plain-text line in /etc/sysctl.conf — remove the line, the value is gone. No recompiled kernels, no -current, no patches. Everything here works on the release you already installed, with the packages the mirrors already serve. No fancy filesystems, no exotic schedulers. The default FFS layout stays; the default services stay. A desktop is the place you should be least creative. Firefox does the media work ; the OS only has to stop tripping it. Note: check every number against your own machine ( sysctl -a prints the current ones). The kernel clamps or rejects values outside its range, and it tells you when it does — listen to it, do not fight it. 02 The values that stop the lag This is the section you came for. Three ceilings cover most desktop slowdowns: file descriptors, the process cap, and the thread cap. A browser is many processes each holding many files when video is rolling; the defaults were sized smaller than that. Sysctl Desktop value Default-ish base Why video lagged kern.maxfiles 10240 7022 Each tab/thread keeps sockets, pipes, media descriptors; the cap lands and the browser queues instead of rendering. kern.maxproc 65000 1310 A modern browser spawns processes per tab. Past the cap, new tabs die or the compositor stalls. kern.maxthread 4096 1024 Media decoding is thread-hungry; when threads get refused, video decodes late — which is the “OS lagging” feel. Apply them live, right now, no reboot: $ doas sysctl kern.maxfiles=10240 $ doas sysctl kern.maxproc=65000 $ doas sysctl kern.maxthread=4096 Then open Firefox, play a video, resize the window, switch tabs. The machine should stay smooth because the browser stopped knocking on a closed ceiling. If a value is refused “Invalid argument” or “Permission denied” , the range on your kernel is different — back off, or read options(4) ; do not shave the kernel. What I am not telling you to change: vm.* percentages, buffer cache ratios, kern.maxclusters beyond sanity, scheduler hacks. On a general-purpose laptop those defaults are right, and turning them is how people “tune” a working system into a mysterious one. Seriously, only three sysctls? For video playback without OS lag, yes in the common case: descriptors, processes and threads are what a browser exhausts first. If your case is different, the evidence is readable: systat vmstat during playback shows you whether the machine is swapping (RAM problem → section 06), starving on descriptors (files problem → this section), or neither (then the lag is mismatched driver rendering → section 04). 03 Testing, then keeping The beauty of sysctls: try, keep, or leave with a one-line difference. Runtime first as above; then, to survive reboots, the same key=value pairs go into /etc/sysctl.conf : # /etc/sysctl.conf — one line each, no 'sysctl' keyword kern.maxfiles=10240 kern.maxproc=65000 kern.maxthread=4096 Confirm the boot result once: $ doas reboot $ sysctl kern.maxfiles kern.maxproc kern.maxthread Discipline that keeps this safe for a normal user: Change one thing at a time and use the machine for an hour. If anything feels strange, delete one line from /etc/sysctl.conf , reboot, done. Keep a note (this page's checklist, or a file) of every line you added. Six months from now “the system changed behaviour” will actually be “past-me added a line”. Do not set values you have no reason for. More is not smoother; mis-sized memory pools are just a new way to be slow. 04 Firefox, tamed Firefox from packages is the right Firefox — it is built against the system's libraries and speaks sndio for audio natively: $ doas pkg_add firefox Video playback on OpenBSD decodes in software through the bundled ffmpeg stack; the machine behind sections 02 and 06 is what makes it smooth. There is one optional forward step: Note (optional): on machines whose DRM driver exposes hardware video decode (newer Intel graphics are the usual candidates), Firefox can attempt VAAPI: about:config → media.ffmpeg.vaapi.enabled → true , restart, and check whether videos actually behave. It is per-profile and revertible with the same switch set back to false . If there is no improvement — or video gets worse — flip it back and move on. No loss. Warn: do not chase acceleration through unofficial builds, forks or scripts pasted from forums. A browser that runs outside the package system is un-signed, un-updated and a genuine security regression on the machine you can least afford to regress. Small habits that keep it fast Keep the profile small: hundreds of dormant tabs cost memory on any OS. Let the package system update it ( pkg_add -u ) instead of living between versions. If the browser itself freezes but the desktop answers, that is an in-browser problem — sections 02/06 will not fix a broken profile; a fresh one will. 05 Audio without crackle sndiod is already running and mixing by default. Desktops rarely need tuning; when video + music at once hiss or crackle under load, the device buffer can grow a little: # /etc/rc.conf.local — only if audio crackles under load sndiod_flags=-b2400 $ doas rcctl set sndiod flags -b2400 $ doas rcctl restart sndiod Bigger buffer = more latency (a few milliseconds you will not notice) in exchange for staying fluid when the CPU spikes. Defaults first; change only what crackles. Per-application volume just works on sndio ; per-app mixers from other systems do not exist here and are not missed. Note: if audio devices change (plug/unplug, monitors with speakers), sndiod re-reads devices on the fly. Persistent weirdness is usually the volume knob of the wrong device, not broken config. 06 RAM arithmetic No sysctl rescues too little RAM. Video in a browser is a few gigabytes of anonymous memory; the page daemon starts clawing pages back as soon as the machine is tight, and that reclaiming is the real “OS is lagging” experience — the system keeps running while it swaps your video in and out. $ systat vm 1 # watch pi/po (pages in/out) during a video 8 GB : fine for one browser session + WM + terminal. 16 GB : the comfortable desktop number. How to be honest about it: play your worst case (video + video call + editor) and watch systat vm . If pi/po churn while the system feels mushy, you need more memory, not more tuning. Swap exists to exist, not to be a second RAM: leave the default swap sized at install time, leave the virtual-memory ratios alone, and treat “ vm.anonmin ”-style advice as something for people with a measurement, not a feeling. Note: if the machine is old-slow rather than out-of-memory, upgrade path is RAM → SSD → patient browser habits. The sysctls of section 02 only remove the artificial ceiling. 07 Trackpads and keyboards These are wsconsctl knobs — same reversibility as sysctls. Trackpad tapping and natural scrolling behaviour live here: $ doas wsconsctl -w mouse.tapping=1 # tap = click, live $ doas wsconsctl -w mouse.scrolling=0 # 0 traditional, 1 natural And to keep them after reboot, /etc/wsconsctl.conf takes the bare key=value lines: # /etc/wsconsctl.conf mouse.tapping=1 mouse.scrolling=0 Keyboard layouts follow the same pattern; list what your console understands and set it live with wsconsctl keyboard.map= ... then persist in the same file. Two knobs on the laptop (tapping + scrolling) cover 90% of the “OpenBSD feels unfinished” first impressions. Warn: do not autoload random X11 driver flags or modeline hacks from forums to fix a trackpad. The wsconsctl route is the project's own and it survives xenodm restarts; the forum route survives nothing. 08 Battery, lid, suspend Laptops get the pleasant part of OpenBSD: suspend ( zzz ) works out of the box, and the lid action is a sysctl: $ apm # battery state + performance mode $ doas apm -A # automatic performance adjustment $ doas sysctl machdep.lidaction=1 # close lid = suspend (1); 0 leaves it alone Persist the lid behaviour in /etc/sysctl.conf like the others: # /etc/sysctl.conf machdep.lidaction=1 Allow yourself to suspend without a password being typed each time — acceptable only for zzz itself: # /etc/doas.conf permit nopass :wheel cmd zzz Warn: permit nopass otherwise gets you a root-shaped hole in the name of convenience. One command, exactly that command. Note: after suspend, if the clock is off, ntpd re-syncs automatically. If keys repeat weirdly until the next reboot, that is your machine's firmware being ancient, not OpenBSD's fault alone — the same happens walking between three other OSes. 09 A window manager that answers cwm ships in base and is the truthful answer to “what WM on OpenBSD”. X as a whole is started by xenodm : $ doas rcctl enable xenodm $ doas rcctl start xenodm And your ~/.xsession simply must point at it (this file is the only thing between you and a black screen; keep it tiny): # ~/.xsession . /etc/X11/xinit/xinitrc.d/40-systray 2>/dev/null || true xsetroot -solid \"#070b12\" exec cwm Why cwm and not something showier: it is keyboard-first, memory-flat, updated with the base system, and sports the most honest manual page in any WM. Window managers from packages (fvwm, i3 and so on) also work — if a package install goes wrong, it is removable and you still have twm and a console. Note: keep xenodm enabled rather than starting X from a bare console every time; multiuser discipline survives by accident otherwise. 10 Fonts and the packages worth having A desktop without good fonts is a desktop you describe as “ugly”. This is fixed by packages, and it cannot break anything: $ doas pkg_add noto-fonts noto-fonts-emoji dejavu-fonts fonts: a full family + emoji covers all web pages you will open. audio/video: nothing extra; ffmpeg rides inside Firefox and friends via packages. tools: curl , git , vim (or neovim), zsh — all from packages, all disposable. updates are one command, run occasionally: pkg_add -u . Note: stay on -release / -stable as a normal user. -current is a full-time hobby; a browser that changes under your video every week is a form of self-harm. 11 The boring parts that matter User discipline: live as a normal user; doas for the few things above. Everything on this page runs through doas, never inside a bare root shell. Email noise: the daily maintenance cron mail tells you about things like “disk nearing capacity”. Read it instead of filtering it: it is the OS whispering. /etc/motd : shorten it. Reclaiming screen inches — not “tuning”, but the daily reward. dmesg and sysctl -a : after every change, compare once before/after before calling it “better”. Feelings lie; diffs do not. Back up the small config: these are now “your” files — /etc/sysctl.conf , /etc/wsconsctl.conf , /etc/doas.conf , ~/.xsession . Four files; save a copy with tar when they feel right. Warn: nothing on this page should push you to enable services from rcctl you cannot name the purpose of. A desktop with 8 enabled daemons is a small server wearing a desktop's face, and it inherits a server's attack surface with none of its pay. 12 Cheat sheet Goal Command Un-stick video ceilings (live) doas sysctl kern.maxfiles=10240 kern.maxproc=65000 kern.maxthread=4096 Keep them over reboots same three pairs, one per line, in /etc/sysctl.conf See current values sysctl kern.maxfiles kern.maxproc kern.maxthread Audio breathing room rcctl set sndiod flags -b2400 && rcctl restart sndiod Trackpad manners doas wsconsctl -w mouse.tapping=1 (+ line in /etc/wsconsctl.conf ) Suspend now / on lid doas zzz / machdep.lidaction=1 Watch memory churn systat vm 1 X with cwm rcctl enable xenodm , exec cwm in ~/.xsession Fonts pkg_add noto-fonts noto-fonts-emoji dejavu-fonts Everything fresh pkg_add -u 13 Your desktop, checked off Progress below is stored in this browser ( localStorage ) only — closing the page keeps it. 0 / 10 RESET sysctl -a captured before any change (your before-picture) kern.maxfiles=10240 applied and kept in /etc/sysctl.conf kern.maxproc=65000 applied and kept kern.maxthread=4096 applied and kept Video in Firefox plays smoothly with tabs switching beside it systat vm watched during playback; pi/po calm (or RAM planned) Audio checked under load; -b2400 applied only if it crackled Trackpad tapping/scroll set via wsconsctl and persisted Lid + suspend + doas nopass for zzz only The four config files copied away once ( sysctl.conf , wsconsctl.conf , doas.conf , ~/.xsession )

ordersAndConscience: Home Monkey Blog · Big Dossier English Português Politics, Law & Justice · Big Dossier Orders and Conscience The same machine, seen from both sides: evil done in the name of the Good, good done in the name of evil — and what the psychology of obedience, moral injury and refusal tells us about the person inside the uniform. Obedience Refusal Moral injury De-escalation Sources Bilingual How to read this dossier You wear a uniform, 15 minutes — read 1 , 2 and 7 . The four questions in section 7 are the part worth memorising. You are a citizen, 20 minutes — read 3 , 4 and 5 . These are the two faces of the same machine, and the bill. You train people, 30 minutes — read 6 , 7 and 8 . Section 8 is the part institutions hate. You have five minutes — section 2 : the answer that the law gave in 1946 and never took back. You want the whole history — read 3 and 4 together, century by century: every order in the first list has a name in the second. 1. How obedience is manufactured No state has ever needed to convince most of its people to be cruel. It only has to arrange the situation so that cruelty looks like procedure. The rest is engineering, and the engineering has been studied for eighty years. The experiments that still explain the office Stanley Milgram's 1963 study at Yale put ordinary volunteers in front of a machine they believed delivered shocks to a stranger. A man in a grey coat said please continue . About sixty-five percent went all the way to the highest switch. When two peers openly refused, obedience collapsed to a small fraction; when the authority left the room, or was replaced by an ordinary man in a shirt, it fell sharply too. The finding was never about Germans, or about evil people: it was about how much the obedience of a normal person depends on the room he is standing in. Solomon Asch showed the same soft machinery with lines of different length: people will deny their own eyes to agree with a group. In the standard experiments about a third of answers followed the majority, and roughly three quarters of participants conformed at least once. Nobody was threatened. Being the only one who disagrees was cost enough. The Stanford prison study of 1971 is still quoted as proof that power corrupts. It should be quoted as a warning about evidence instead: recordings released decades later show coaching, rehearsed lines and a guard role played to please the researcher. The lesson survives, but inverted — a study can be built to produce the result the designer wants, which is exactly what an institution does when it dresses a decision as a policy. The four tools of distance Albert Bandura described moral disengagement as a set of switches that let a person do harm and keep a clean self-image. They appear in every bureaucracy, in every language: Moral justification — the cause is Good, therefore the act is permitted. God, nation, order, security, peace, revolution. Euphemism — pacification, collateral damage, enhanced interrogation, redistribution, cleaning the area. The word arrives before the act and hides it while it happens. Diffusion of responsibility — I do not make policy, I apply it. The signature is one of forty signatures. The order came from above, and above is a committee. Dehumanisation — they are not like us, they are a mob, they are numbers on a list, they are a risk score. A soldier , a police officer and a clerk in an office are trained in the first two and protected by the third. The fourth one is announced on the radio. Nobody starts at the grave Complicity is built in steps small enough to be deniable: deliver the message, keep the file, sign the transfer, do not ask why the list is shorter. Each step makes the next one cheaper, because refusing now would mean admitting what the previous step was. This is why the first refusal is the strongest and the last one is almost impossible. Reserve Police Battalion 101, Józefów, July 1942: the commander offered those who did not feel able to shoot the option of stepping out. Most men still killed. The ones who stepped out were not punished, were not transferred, and were not killed. Refusal was possible — that is the uncomfortable, important fact that the defence "there was no choice" cannot survive. The price of being the one who asks Against the moral cost stands a small, ordinary, human cost: transfer, mockery, no promotion, the locker room going quiet, the feeling of being the problem for the group. Armies and police forces have always known this and have used it as a free enforcement mechanism. Distrust is cheaper than discipline. The counterweights are documented too: visible identification , written records , an independent complaint route, and a chain of command that publicly protects the person who said no. The soft machine Modern obedience rarely arrives as a shout. It arrives as a screen: a risk score, a quota of fines, an automated flag, a list of names, a pushback order written in administrative language. The old sentence survives intact, only the grammar changed: I only followed orders became I only applied the rule . The distance grew from an office wall to an interface, and distance is the ingredient that does the work. 2. What the law already decided The excuse that emptied the twentieth century — Befehl ist Befehl , an order is an order — was answered in writing, with sources that any uniformed person can read in ten minutes. Nuremberg Principle IV (formulated by the UN International Law Commission, 1950): acting under the order of a government or a superior does not relieve a person of responsibility under international law, provided a moral choice was in fact possible to him . That last clause is the whole doctrine. It does not say obey is always criminal; it says obedience is not a shield. Rome Statute, article 33 (1998): superior orders are not a defence when the order is manifestly unlawful — and orders to commit genocide or crimes against humanity are, by definition, manifestly unlawful. Customary international humanitarian law, rule 155 : obeying a superior order does not relieve a subordinate of criminal responsibility if he knew the act was unlawful, or should have known. Conscience is a protected right : article 18 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights protects freedom of thought, conscience and religion; the UN human rights system reads conscientious objection to military service as a legitimate exercise of that right. The European Court of Human Rights said it plainly in Bayatyan v. Armenia (2011), after decades in which it had avoided the question. In Portugal , article 41(6) of the Constitution states that the right to conscientious objection is guaranteed in the terms of the law — a sentence written in 1976, two years after a war ended and a regime fell. Two honest qualifications, because a dossier that only sells comfort is useless. The first: the law protects you afterwards, sometimes. On the day, in the corridor, with a supervisor waiting for your answer, the law is not in the room. Only procedure and allies are. Section 7 is therefore about procedure, not principles. The second: "manifestly unlawful" is a higher bar than "unpleasant" or "pointless" or "politically embarrassing". An order you dislike is not an illegal order. The test is narrower than conscience and wider than rank, and it is worth learning precisely because it protects the refuser from becoming merely insubordinate. Never hand your conscience to someone else to hold. 3. Face one — evil in the name of the Good Every century repeats the same sentence: the cause is Good, therefore the act must be permitted. What follows is the file, not the sermon. Figures follow the historians and the commissions of inquiry; where estimates differ, they differ, and the difference is noted. All Before 1900 1900–1945 1945–1990 After 1990 36 / 36 1099 · Jerusalem After the walls of the First Crusade 's prize fell, the population of the city was killed in the name of God. Medieval chroniclers claimed tens of thousands; modern estimates are lower, still in the low thousands. The slaughter was described by the winners as an act of purification. 1209 · Béziers The Albigensian Crusade against the Cathars. The line kill them all, God will know his own is attributed to a papal legate and may be legend — the sack of the city was not. Crusades against Christians, once started, never paused for a theological check. 1478–1834 · Spanish Inquisition An institution built to punish belief, with a bureaucracy, a filing system, an interrogation practice and a public ceremony. Most of the accused were never executed; the machinery that made the threat credible was the point. 1492 · Spain, and 1496 · Portugal Jews expelled from Spain, then forced to convert or leave in Portugal. An administrative decision, taken in law, executed by officials, with the property of the expelled staying behind. 1885–1908 · Congo Free State Leopold II of Belgium ran a private colony as a rubber concession. Hostages were taken to force quotas; hands were cut as proof of ammunition used. Roger Casement's 1904 consular report and E. D. Morel's campaign dragged it into the light. Estimates of population loss run from one million to several million, and the disagreements are about method, not about cruelty. 1904–1908 · German South-West Africa Von Trotha's extermination order against the Herero, then the Nama. Roughly four fifths of the Herero died; the survivors were used as forced labour. Germany formally recognised the killings as genocide in 2021, and agreed to a fund of about €1.1 billion. An estimated 1.5 million people, out of the war 's chaos, by design. More than thirty states and the overwhelming majority of historians call it genocide; the denial continues as a state policy, which is itself part of the file. 1917 · Chemin des Dames After a failed French offensive, soldiers refused to attack again. Thousands were involved, hundreds sentenced, dozens executed. Quotas were assigned to regions.
